type:
∀ {α : Type*} (encode : α → _root_.List _root_.Bool)
    (decode : _root_.List _root_.Bool → _root_.Option α)
    (hInjective : _root_.Function.Injective encode)
    (hDecode : ∀ x : α, decode (encode x) = _root_.Option.some x)
    (hInvalid : ∀ w : _root_.List _root_.Bool,
      w ∉ _root_.Set.range encode → decode w = _root_.Option.none)
    (A : _root_.Set α),
    _root_.ComputablyEnumerableSet encode decode hInjective hDecode hInvalid A →
    _root_.Set.Infinite A →
    ∃ f : _root_.Nat → α,
      _root_.Computable (fun n : _root_.Nat => encode (f n)) ∧
      _root_.Function.Injective f ∧ _root_.Set.range f = A
sourceReason: Alphabeta Math’s shared-library item thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations states the theorem for arbitrary effectively encoded sets. Page 4 of arXiv:2609.00419v1 uses the natural-number instance. The translation uses the same binary encoding and decoding convention as ComputablyEnumerableSet. The article-specific Research Portal and designated defect report both returned HTTP 404, so any correction remains unverified. https://alphabetamath.cc/item/thm-infinite-ce-sets-have-computable-injective-enumerations
